title: Prenatal Exposure to Phthalates and Anogenital Distance in Male Infants from a Low-Exposed Danish Cohort (2010-2012).
ehr_evidence: The study was based on data from the Odense Child Cohort. Fasting spot urine samples were collected at approximately GA 28 weeks before 0930 hours and stored in freezers at the Odense Patient data Explorative Network (OPEN).
summary: Prospective cohort study investigating the association between maternal urinary phthalate metabolite concentrations during pregnancy and anogenital distance (AGD) and penile width in male offspring at 3 months of age.
key_findings: No dose-dependent association was found between any prenatal phthalate metabolite and AGD or penile width (p > 0.05).

Mean AGDas was lower for boys in the second, third, and fourth quartiles of MEP compared with the first quartile [–0.64 mm (95% CI: –2.52, 1.23), –1.68 mm (95% CI: –3.56, 0.20), and –1.37 mm (95% CI: –3.27, 0.54)], but differences were not statistically significant.
Maternal ∑DiNPm and ∑DEHPm levels in higher quartiles were associated with shorter AGD compared to the first quartile, but associations were not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
data_source_type: cohort biospecimen collection and clinical examination
population: pregnant women and male infants in Odense, Denmark (2010–2012)
limitations: single spot urine sample may not reflect fetal exposure in sensitive developmental windows
potential residual confounding by co-exposure to other environmental chemicals, lifestyle, or health behavior
selection bias with only 42% participation and better-educated participants
temporal and seasonal variation in phthalate levels
fasting state may affect urine concentration
